rituals.title: AROUSAL PREDICTION
rituals.mission: Turn calm-seeking into a falsifiable forecast.
rituals.play: Choose HIGHER, LOWER, or SAME, then engage with the room for twenty seconds before checking once.
rituals.win: State change becomes an observation instead of a target.
rituals.mind_bend: Making one arousal forecast and checking only at the end exposes the gap between predicted activation and actual short-term change without contaminating it through constant monitoring.

GAME
AROUSAL PREDICTION

MISSION
Turn calm-seeking into a falsifiable forecast.

ONE RULE
One forecast and one check.

PLAY
Choose HIGHER, LOWER, or SAME, then engage with the room for twenty seconds before checking once.

TWIST
No mid-interval monitoring.

WIN
State change becomes an observation instead of a target.

MIND BEND
Making one arousal forecast and checking only at the end exposes the gap between predicted activation and actual short-term change without contaminating it through constant monitoring.

rituals.title: EMOTION WORD BAN
rituals.mission: Force raw description.
rituals.rule: Use only location, movement, urge, and context.
rituals.play: For five seconds, describe what is present without saying anxious, angry, sad, guilty, etc.
rituals.win: The state is experienced without its usual category vocabulary.
rituals.mind_bend: An emotion can be described through location, movement, urge and context before any emotion word appears, revealing how much experience exists underneath the label.

rituals.title: EMOTION ORDER
rituals.mission: Use temporal ordering rather than distraction.
rituals.play: If two feelings are present, identify which one arrived first and which followed, without deciding which matters more.
rituals.twist: If order is unclear, mark UNKNOWN.
rituals.win: You can tell which of two coexisting feelings appeared first.
rituals.mind_bend: Two emotions can coexist while their order of arrival remains uncertain, showing that emotional sequence is a separate fact from emotional intensity.

rituals.title: EMOTION ACTION BLOCK
rituals.mission: Separate state from action.
rituals.play: Name the action tendency once, then wait five seconds without doing it.
rituals.win: Emotion remains while its preferred action is withheld.
rituals.mind_bend: An emotion can produce a clear action urge while the action remains unperformed, exposing feeling, impulse and behaviour as three distinguishable stages.

rituals.title: ILLUSORY CORRELATION
rituals.mission: See whether a striking pairing feels more common than it really is.
rituals.rule: Count occurrences before trusting the impression.
rituals.play: Use four cases: A+calm, A+tense, B+calm, B+tense—one of each. First notice any intuitive group-feeling link, then count the actual pairings.
rituals.twist: The counts get the final say, not vividness.
rituals.win: A felt association can disappear when the co-occurrence table is made explicit.
rituals.mind_bend: A vivid pairing can feel strongly associated even when balanced counts say otherwise, exposing correlation impressions as vulnerable to salience and selective memory.

rituals.win: Identical arousal can support different interpretations.
rituals.mind_bend: The same imagined feeling can acquire a different meaning in another harmless context, revealing how emotional interpretation depends on situation rather than sensation alone.

rituals.title: URGE + CHOICE

rituals.twist: End the round at that first direction change; do not keep monitoring.

You catch the urge's first loss of upward momentum even if the urge is still present.

PAUSE
If the urge could put you or someone else at risk, create real distance from means/cues and involve another person or professional support; do not rely on this game alone.
rituals.mind_bend: The instant rising intensity first levels or falls marks a real change in the urge’s trajectory, proving escalation can end while substantial activation remains.

rituals.title: POINT-OF-NO-RETURN
rituals.mission: Find the first real commitment point inside a habit.
rituals.play: Take one harmless habit. Mentally list its first few physical microsteps—reach, pick up, open, move—and identify the earliest step that makes continuation noticeably harder to reverse.
rituals.twist: Move your intervention point one step earlier than that commitment point.
rituals.win:
The habit gains a concrete pre-commitment point where interruption is easier.

PAUSE
If the urge could put you or someone else at risk, create real distance from means/cues and involve another person or professional support; do not rely on this game alone.
rituals.mind_bend: A habit contains a physical commitment point after which stopping becomes harder, revealing why intervention is more powerful one microstep earlier.

rituals.win: Access to action becomes harder in the real environment.
rituals.mind_bend: Increasing distance from harmful means changes which actions are immediately available; safety can therefore be built into the physical choice architecture.

rituals.win: Active retrieval can strengthen later access differently from passive restudy.
rituals.mind_bend: Actively retrieving studied material can strengthen later memory more than simply rereading it again, revealing recall effort as part of learning rather than merely a test after learning.

rituals.win: A second target can become harder to notice when it arrives soon after the first.
